messages:
sam: deploy-bot just halted the canary publish for service-x (staging -> canary). saw `provenance: missing` in the webhook. Deploy bot output pasted below. Can we decide quick whether to pin previous digest or attempt an emergency republish?

deploy-bot: publish halted by provenance-guard (code 422).
  image: public.ecr.aws/redwood/service-x:staging-canary-20260321
  reason: attestation-missing (expected cosign.attestations.kms)
  actions: [pin-old-digest, republish-with-attest, schedule-republish-in-window]

alex: ugh. was smoke run green against the canary image?

sam: yes, quick smoke passed on the ephemeral node (logs showed list endpoints ok). failing step is before the deployment — ECR reject on missing KMS annotation during attestation step.

maria: so two choices: 1) pin the previous digest for the in-flight canary (keeps traffic on old image) and unblock the change window; OR 2) attempt to re-run publisher with KMS attach + cosign attestation now. Republish may succeed but could take 10-20m and might re-trigger rate limits.

raj: if we republish we need to ensure the key used for cosign is the rotated key (we had a key rotation yesterday). quick check: `cosign verify-attestation --key k8s://projects/redwood/keys/cosign-rotation` failed earlier for this build.

alex: we need the release notes update either way. If we pin, we must annotate the rollback in notes and schedule a republish during the nightly change window. If we republish now and it succeeds, we still need a small amend to release notes mentioning republish for provenance.

sam: I'm leaning pin + schedule republish during 02:00-04:00 UTC window. Minimizes risk for customer-facing flakiness.

maria: +1. Also add a one-liner in the release notes: "Canary deploy held due to missing provenance attestation; pinned to previous digest; republish scheduled during maintenance window."

raj: quick command if we try republish (do NOT run without TO):
```
# re-run publisher with explicit key and annotation
./publish.sh --image service-x --tag staging-canary-20260321 --cosign-key k8s://projects/redwood/keys/cosign-rotation --annotate kms=true
```
If key not present on the runner, republish will fail and we will be back here.

deploy-bot: action executed: pin-old-digest -> pinned public.ecr.aws/redwood/service-x@sha256:2b9f... (previous canary digest). TTL: immediate rollback block cleared.

sam: ok pinned. I'll open a follow-up ticket to republish with correct key and KMS annotation in the 02:00 UTC window. Assigning to @raj to validate key availability on the publisher runners.

raj: I will validate key access and add an automated preflight that runs `cosign verify-attestation` against the artifact before publisher tries to finalize. If that fails we should fail fast instead of halfway through.

alex: nice. sam, please add release notes line and ping cs/support about the pinned canary + expected republish time. We should also note the customer-visible impact: none (traffic stayed on previous digest) but callout for internal audit.

maria: adding a short postmortem checklist in the ticket: key-rotation verification, publisher preflight, and release note template update. :memo:

sam: done — ticket: RE-4456 (republish + preflight). I've updated the release note draft and included the pinned digest and link to this thread.

alex: thanks team. leaving this thread open until republish completes. If anyone wants to attempt emergency republish before window, call it out here with reason. :raised_hands:
